canonical_statement: The study examined 12-month changes in body composition and bone mineral density in people with obesity and type 1 diabetes treated with GLP-1RA alone or dual GIP/GLP-1RA therapy.
The study also explored whether changes in fat mass, lean mass, and bone outcomes differed according to the percentage of body weight lost.
This was a prospective observational study conducted in routine clinical care at the Dasman Diabetes Institute.
The Institutional Review Board of the Dasman Diabetes Institute approved the study under RA HM-2020-018, and the study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki.

Eligible participants were adults aged at least 18 years with obesity and documented type 1 diabetes by ADA criteria who received GLP-1RA alone or dual GIP/GLP-1RA therapy as part of routine DAFNE clinical management.

inclusion_criteria: Documented type 1 diabetes by ADA criteria

canonical_statement: Treatment followed standard clinical protocols for obesity, including gradual dose escalation to minimise side effects and improve tolerability.

Demographic, clinical, and biochemical variables including age, sex, body weight, HbA1c, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation were extracted from electronic health records at baseline and 12 months.

Body composition and bone parameters were assessed annually by whole-body DXA using Lunar iDXA with enCORE software, quantifying regional and total fat mass, tissue fat percentage, lean mass, BMC, and BMD.
Android fat was defined as fat accumulation in the abdominal region between the ribs and pelvis, with the lower boundary at the iliac crest.

concept.text: Android fat

outcome.definition: Fat accumulation in the abdominal region between the ribs and pelvis, lower boundary at iliac crest

canonical_statement: Gynoid fat was defined as fat distribution around the hips and upper thighs.

concept.text: Gynoid fat

outcome.definition: Fat distribution around the hips and upper thighs

canonical_statement: Full-cohort baseline-to-12-month changes were analysed with GLM repeated-measures tests adjusted for age and sex; percentage changes and 95% confidence intervals were estimated with linear mixed models adjusted for age and sex.
Observed power was calculated for outcome analyses, with values of at least 0.80 considered indicative of adequate statistical power.
Spearman correlations were used to assess associations between weight loss and body-composition outcomes.

Participants were stratified by percentage weight loss into less than 5%, 5%-10%, and greater than 10% groups; within- and between-stratum changes were analysed with GLM repeated measures and ANCOVA adjusted for age and sex.
The study cohort comprised 33 males (47.1%) and 37 females (52.9%).

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that 12 months of GLP-1RA alone or dual GIP/GLP-1RA therapy was associated with clinically meaningful weight loss, improved glycaemic control, preferential fat-mass reduction, modest lean-mass loss, and preservation of total BMD in people with obesity and type 1 diabetes.

The authors concluded that people achieving greater than 10% weight loss had the greatest metabolic benefit without a significant deterioration in total BMD or BMC, although lean-mass loss was greater.

source_anchor.paragraph: Bone health and weight-loss strata discussion

canonical_statement: The authors stated that future randomized controlled trials with larger samples and longer follow-up are warranted to confirm these findings.
The observational design precludes causal inference, and the absence of a control group limits definitive attribution of observed changes to GLP-1RA or dual GIP/GLP-1RA therapy.
Sample sizes within the weight-loss strata were relatively small and may have reduced statistical power for some outcomes.
A 12-month follow-up may not be long enough to detect changes in bone mineral density.

No significant change in total-body BMD should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of stability at hip or spine sites because regional BMD may decline without measurable change in total-body BMD.
Changes in body size and tissue thickness during large weight change may artificially alter DXA-derived bone area and may contribute to opposite-direction changes in BMD and BMC.
Dietary intake, physical activity, and changes in insulin dosing were unavailable and may have influenced body-composition outcomes.
Adverse-event collection was limited to severe hypoglycaemia and diabetic ketoacidosis; gastrointestinal symptoms and other adverse events were not captured.

Study manpower was funded by the Kuwait Foundation of Advancement of Science and the Ministry of Health, Kuwait; the authors stated that the funding agency did not influence study design, data analysis, interpretation, or report preparation.

Carel W. le Roux reported personal fees from Boehringer Ingelheim, Eli Lilly, GI Dynamics, Gila Pharmaceuticals, Herbalife, Johnson & Johnson, Keyron, Novo Nordisk, and Zealand Pharma outside the submitted work; research funding from MRC, NIHR, Jon Moulton Charitable Foundation, Fractyl, Gila, Randox, and Novo Nordisk; and shareholding in the Beyond BMI clinic.

Scientific and medical researchers can request access to clinical study data after publication in accordance with the Dasman Diabetes Institute policy on transparency and publication of clinical study data.
